governanceNotes: D1 batch 63 (2026-09-26): one bounded association edge authored - necrobiosis-lipoidica to squamous-cell-carcinoma (rank 1) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The proposition rests on the systematic review of cutaneous malignancies arising in NLD (PMID 40538107), the fatal SCC case in a decades-long ulcerated NLD field (PMID 30870808), and the ulcerated-NLD SCC case (PMID 24373177).

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-26: (i) evidence class - a systematic review collating case reports and individual cases; no incidence denominator exists anywhere in the located base; (ii) substrate specificity - malignancy arises in the long-standing ulcerated subset of NLD, not in intact plaques, so the edge's scope is the ulcerated field; (iii) publication bias - fatal and aggressive courses are preferentially reported; (iv) latency - decades-long ulceration is the reported pattern but transformation latency is unquantified per lesion.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Squamous cell carcinoma arising in long-standing ulcerated necrobiosis lipoidica is documented at systematic-review and case level: the systematic review of cutaneous malignancies arising in necrobiosis lipoidica summarizes the characteristics, management, and outcomes of malignancies developing within NLD lesions (PMID 40538107), the fatal case report documents SCC developing in a decades-long ulcerated NLD field in a diabetic patient and frames non-healing NLD ulcers as demanding a high index of suspicion for malignancy (PMID 30870808), and the case report documents SCC arising in ulcerated necrobiosis lipoidica (PMID 24373177); recorded as documented association only.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the anchors are a review collating case-class evidence and individual case reports arising in long-standing ulcerated plaques, so whether any individual carcinoma is attributable to the necrobiosis-lipoidica field requires individual dermatopathological attribution with chronic-wound, actinic, and radiation exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Decades of non-healing ulceration within the necrobiosis lipoidica plaque drive chronic inflammatory signaling and regenerative turnover in the wound bed so malignant transformation to squamous cell carcinoma results, the chronic-wound field route stated in the fatal case framing that the NLD ulcer bed provides a favorable environment for SCC formation, but whether this route produced any individual carcinoma remains hypothesized until lesion and pathology records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at systematic-review-of-cases plus individual case class only: no cohort quantifies SCC incidence in NLD populations, the malignancy literature is case reports collated by review with publication bias toward severe outcomes, and the transformation latency in any individual plaque is unquantified.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No located cohort quantifies squamous cell carcinoma incidence in necrobiosis lipoidica; the systematic review collates case-class evidence where publication bias toward fatal or aggressive courses is expected; duration of ulceration before transformation varies widely across reports; and malignancy in other chronic wounds overlaps the differential.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Marjolin ulcer arising in burn scars, venous stasis ulcers, or hidradenitis sinuses
actinic keratosis and field cancerization in sun-damaged skin
SCC arising in diabetic foot ulcers or chronic osteomyelitis sinuses
basal cell carcinoma and other cutaneous malignancies in the NLD field

evidenceGaps: No located cohort quantifies squamous cell carcinoma incidence in necrobiosis lipoidica; the systematic review collates case-class evidence where publication bias toward fatal or aggressive courses is expected; duration of ulceration before transformation varies widely across reports; and malignancy in other chronic wounds overlaps the differential.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at systematic-review-of-cases plus case class with the incidence-unquantified limit carried openly: the systematic review documents cutaneous malignancies arising within NLD lesions (PMID 40538107), the fatal case frames decades-long ulcerated NLD as a high-index-of-suspicion malignancy field (PMID 30870808), and the ulcerated-NLD SCC case corroborates the transformation pattern (PMID 24373177); because no located cohort quantifies incidence and the evidence class is publication-prone case material, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through dated biopsy of non-healing NLD ulcers with chronic-wound and actinic exclusion.
